payload.name: Extract explicit advice between speakers
payload.description: When during extraction one speaker explicitly suggests, recommends, or advises a course of action to another speaker, create a candidate memory for that suggestion even if phrased tentatively.
content: During extraction, treat explicit advice, recommendations, or suggestions from one speaker to another as durable, memory-worthy facts even when phrased tentatively (e.g., 'Maybe look into...', 'Consider...', 'You might try...').
Create a candidate memory capturing the adviser, the recipient, and the advised action so the suggestion can be retrieved later.

solves: During extraction, explicit suggestions or recommendations that one speaker gives to another were missed, so the fact was never stored and later questions about the advice could not be answered. The reusable mechanism is that advice phrased tentatively ('Maybe look into...', 'You should try...') is still a durable fact about the relationship between participants. This rule applies to any future session where a participant gives advice to another and a later question may ask about it.
